chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you sits for food, let him sit the sitting of a servant, and let not one of you place one leg over the other, nor sit cross-legged, for it is a sitting that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dislikes and He detests its doer.'

key_terms.جِلْسَةَ الْعَبْدِ: the sitting of a servant (humble posture)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended sitting posture for eating in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi traces the etiquette of dining back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and ultimately to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS), emphasizing that the 'posture of the servant' reflects humility and gratitude. It specifically warns against the 'cross-legged' or 'kingly' pose (tarabbu'), linking physical demeanor to spiritual state by noting that Allah detests this arrogant posture. This guidance underscores the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) as an extension of worship, where bodily conduct mirrors inner submission.
